Viper Dead-On Tournament Bristle Steel Tip Dartboard Set with Staple-Free Bullseye, Metal Triangular Spider Wire for Reduced Bounce Outs and Increased Scoring; High-Grade Self-Healing Sisal Board The dead-on viper sisal fiber dartboard is a classic dartboard that you will likely see in your local bar or pub. The spider, or the metal that separates the segments (numbers and colors), is angled on each side. Therefore, if a dart barely hits the side of the spider then it will be directed to hit the sisal fibers. The angled spider helps reduce the number of bounce backs. However, you should notice that the spider has "staples" that go over the metal bar on both sides. If you do not like this aspect of the dartboard then you can spend an extra $10-$15 bucks and upgrade to the viper spider dartboard. Either board is a great addition to your home game room or man (or woman) cave. Great board. Made in Taiwan.

[[ASIN:B000UV57DE Viper Razorback Sisal/Bristle Steel Tip Dartboard with Staple-Free Spider]]

Dual Ab Wheel, Exercise And Fitness Wheel With Easy Grip Handles For Core Training And Abdominal Workout This ab wheel isn't anything too fancy. It's just another tool to help build your six pack. However, if using an ab roller is your thing, this is the one to go with.

My gym has some different ab wheels that all get the job done. But they don't have one of these, which I think feels better and provides for a better ab workout. It requires some assembly but it's relatively easy. Just make sure when you put the handles on that you align the finger grips so they both face the same way. Otherwise you will have to fight the grips off and redo them. It also takes a little bit of effort to get the grips on!

The wheel has a nice rubber texture that sticks to the floor so it won't come out from under you or slide around. The handles feel good and provide for a nice grip. This product also comes with a short paper providing some information on how to use it, but it should be rather self explained.

However, do not expect to get a six pack from using this ab wheel alone. This is merely just another tool to help you work your abs. In reality, you need to be working your abs with several different exercises. So keep in mind that this will be just one more tool in your toolbox. It is not the "key" to six pack abs.

Flash Personal Cooking System An absolutely awesome cooking system. Fast, fast, fast! Our initial use for the system will be to boil water for single serve instant coffee packets and to re-hydrate freeze dried food which will keep us and perhaps others happy while camping with the scouts.

Here's a common sense but helpful hint for someone using the Jetboil system for the first time - a no-brainer for anyone who has already cooked with this system:

- If you're just boiling water to pour into another vessel or coffee cup for example, go ahead and fully snap the lid on before beginning your boil. You can conveniently pour through the sipping hole.
- If you're boiling water for the purpose of adding food to the pot such as ramen for example, either lay the lid loosely on top or leave it off altogether.

Why? Because once you snap the lid all the way on and the contents come to a boil you'll burn your fingers trying to get it off unless you use a hot pad or other insulating material.

Highly recommended.

EXERPEUTIC EXERWORK 2000i Bluetooth Folding Exercise Desk Bike with 24 Workout Programs and Free App Ordered in October and it is now February. 4 months of use. Sort of.
The exercise-work-bike took a total of 3 days to put together, and had I been doing it alone, I probably never would have gotten it. There is some form of blue “insta-glue” on the pedal screws that made them nearly impossible to screw in. 3 neighborhood kids and teenagers tried their best to help a lady out, but to no avail. Eventually, I hung my head in shame and begged the assistance of male-friend to demonstrate his masculinity and wield tools to get the pedal screwed in.
I am 5’8. That’s 68 inches or about 172cm.
The next issue came when I realized that even at the lowest adjustment, the one recommended for 5’1-5’4 heights, I still struggled to reach the pedals, sitting with my back comfortably against the backrest. If I scooched forward just enough that half my cheeks were off the front of the seat I could reach the pedals, the backrest, and still use the desk for my laptop! But the desk was still a bit high, so I used the tilt-a-table adjustment to relax my wrists and type with perfectly non-ergonomical T-Rex arms.
And now the clunking noise. I can’t stand it. It started off quiet, but after maybe 100 miles of use, it makes a clunking noise from the pedals and no matter how many times I tighten the bolts (almost to stripping them), the seat keeps wobbling and the handle bars offer very little support.

Overall, as a workout bike, it give options that a regular bike doesn’t have—a table.
As for the rest, I am very unhappy with the very little use I got out of it, the lack of structural support for a solid working/workout of cycling, and how fast it has started having issues.

The first thing I did was charge the batteries. Don't forget to remove the cardboard cover in the battery compartment on top of the second battery that disconnects the power while in shipping. Speaking of the power and switch, this is an easy push switch with a light touch. The four brightness settings are by touching the switch each time for a bright or less bright illumination. Wurkkos has a wonderful design for these 4 settings. You can turn the flashlight off by lightly short pressing the button and that brightness setting will stay for the next time you turn it on. The attachment cord included is also good quality and is comfortable and adjustable for holding or carrying the flashlight and underwater.

The power in this flashlight is amazing, and you do not want to look directly into the lens set on the high setting as it is so bright. On testing distance, I could see 100 yards far into our wooded area and way on top of the 80-foot tall oak trees. Imagine the brightness for deep scuba diving or having to change a prop on your boat at night. On land the flashlight does get warm on high beam for 5 minutes but cools off quickly. I really praise this company for making such an excellent product. This model is nothing short of perfection. The handle grip is comfortable to hold. We have owned a Wurkkos 5950 lumens for 6 months and use it all the time without any problems. If I have any problems with this model, I will update. Right now it is of value and a precision build!!
text_fidelity_b: Wurkkos DL30 Scuba Diving Flashlight - Scuba Dive Light Super Bright Max 3600 Lumen with 5000K 90CRI,100m Underwater Flashlight IPX-8 Waterproof Submersible Flashlight with USB Charger

M48 Tactical Tomahawk Military Axe - Green/Black with Compass & Sheath | 3 ⅞” Cast Stainless Steel Axe | Piercing Spike | Nylon Cord Wrapped Fiberglass Handle | Camping and Tactical Gear | 15” Length I collect knives and hawks. There are two ways that I judge the effectiveness of any sharp tool. Number One is how it stacks up to a good machete. At this point if I could only take one blade into the wilderness, it would be a high quality machete. It has reach and a long cutting surface, is fundamental in design, and can create a large protected area around the user. In addition it cuts through things easily and doesn't typically get hung up in/on the target, unlike other implements. Number Two is judging how I would feel if I were threatened with the tool. It does look wicked, it has two effective blades, it comes sharp(!), can be swung in any direction, and is well built. It's inherent light weight will allow a lot of use before arm fatigue sets in, but it does have some negatives.

On the con side, it is short and its lightness doesn't make it feel substantial in my hand. The cutting surface is much smaller than that of a good machete and of course you can't really stab with it. It is a swinging tool that will allow an experienced fighter to step inside of the swing. Although I haven't tested it, it's hard for me to believe that it can stand up to the abuse that a large man can generate. The M48 probably wouldn't last long against a hard target (breaching doors or cutting wood or metal) but it should prove to be easy to carry and extremely effective against a soft target. I certainly wouldn't want to be hit with it. The best part of the M48 is the value. It is simply one of the most cost effective blades that I have ever bought. And darn, it just looks and feels cool!
text_fidelity_b: M48 Tactical Tomahawk Military Axe - Green/Black with Compass & Sheath | 3 ⅞” Cast Stainless Steel Axe | Piercing Spike | Nylon Cord Wrapped Fiberglass Handle | Camping and Tactical Gear | 15” Length

Lifestyle by Focus Electric Travel Cooler/Warmer Portable Camping Cooler Hard Cooler Ice Chest Roller Wheeled Cooler for Car, Home, Beach, Fishing, Camping, Party (Blue) Large 48 Quart, Holds 60 cans So far, I am underwhelmed. I purchased this in advance of a cross-country trip and an extended stay in a budget hotel that doesn't have a room fridge - hence the choice of dual power source. Being the prudent sort, I plugged it in at home to see whether it really would cool down to 40 degrees. House was 75 degrees, cooler after running all night was 55 degrees, at best. I'll probably keep it, and maybe as a beer or cola cooler it's fine, but as for being able to keep perishables such as eggs, milk, lunch meat and cheese in the hotel, or in transit for 1000 miles, for that matter, I'm not sure it's worth the risk of food poisoning to rely on its cooling capability. It's also smaller inside than I was expecting.

Update: On a second, and much longer, trip, I took this along, mostly for refrigeration in transit, but then when I reached my destination, I found that the full-size fridge was on the blink, so I plugged this in and it kept stuff reasonably cold, including the return trip, although still not much lower than 40-degrees. All told, some of the stuff I carried with me was still good when I got back home eleven days later, and maybe some of that was due to having also packed big bottles of frozen drinking water (ice) and starting out with other frozen foods; maybe some of it was due to my travel being in weather that was at freezing or below and the cooler rode for part of the trip in an unheated truck boot. All that being said, I still wouldn't be totally reliant on it in the summer, and would still pack the bottled ice - which is also a good way to gauge just how well the cooler is doing its job.
text_fidelity_b: Lifestyle by Focus Electric Travel Cooler/Warmer Portable Camping Cooler Hard Cooler Ice Chest Roller Wheeled Cooler for Car, Home, Beach, Fishing, Camping, Party (Blue) Large 48 Quart, Holds 60 cans

text_fidelity_a:
SUV Tent Car Camping Car Tent - Tailgate Tent SUV Tents for Camping, PU4000mm Waterproof, 1-4 Person Sleeping Capacity, Car Tents for Automobiles Car Awning My wife and I are not campers, but when we get out to the beach and parks we like to have something that provides shade and privacy. Where umbrellas and some sun shades are good, we'd been keeping our eyes open for something that might go on the car - expanding our options - and so when I had the chance to grab this SUV Tent Car Camping Car Tent I took it. So far we are pleased... but have a couple... concerns.

It's been a few weeks since we got this SUV Tent Car Camping Car Tent and after having several plans and attempts at even just testing it derailed by weather and wind, we finally had a chance to set it up in a parking lot - not at all ideal, but we at least got to see if it's what we were hoping for. With the weather changing we should be out on the beach sooner than later and we ARE feeling positive this SUV Tent Car Camping Car Tent will be a great addition to our gear.

1. It comes in a nice green bag to fit the tent and support items (poles, stakes).
Pro: It's a great bag to a point, matches the tent, and should make it easier to get this thing around.
Con: It JUST fits the gear so you have to get that tent back down tight. The tent set is heavier than we expected. Not so much we can't get it to the beach - but in that case we'll be with the car - in other words, you'll notice the weight. We do have a wagon we use for longer hauls.

2. It is mainly for the car or truck attachment, but we think we could use it on its own.
Pro: It would be nice to have it stand alone for those times we don't have the car access, and we THINK we could do that.
Con: There is a big hole where it would attach to the car. Would be nice if they had another layer similar to the front awning that you could use - or like the netting - and allow you to enclose the back as well. But alas, it's going to be open.
We are not sure how strong or sturdy it'll be without the car to support it - especially in any kind of wind.

3. Putting it up: not too bad.
Pro: Instructions are average, but there is some level of initiative here that helps get it up.
The poles are easy to put together
The poles are - mostly - easily inserted into the tent and - with two people.
The tent is made sturdily enough that it should last a decent amount of time - holding the poles in their track and forming the tent.
There seems to be enough pieces to give it good form and maintain that.
The straps to hold it to the car are pretty good and one can adapt - for example it says to attach to a roof rack, which we do not have, so we went with putting them into the door of the car and this held them securely and easily.
Con: We had both looked at the pics on the product page so knew what it should look like, but the instructions are average at best.

NOTE: We (again) were unable to get to the beach or park to try this, so it was set up on the edge of a parking lot with fairly bad grass. So we did NOT actually extend it 100% and lock it down nor did we step inside so as not to damage it. But from all we did do, it DOES appear like it will be a great option for us and that it will stay upright.

4. Laying it out & materials
Pro: In a parking lot it was fine, but of course we were being kind to it, trying not to damage it. The materials seem strong enough to take that kind of set up, but would be nicer all around on grass or sand.
The materials of the tent are nice - we like the bright green which will make it easy to spot.
The poles seem well made.
Con: While the tent, poles, and stakes seem like they are well made and with decent materials, we noticed that upon returning everything to the bag, the bag's stitching was already tearing. This was NOT there when we began and my wife felt popping as she pushed everything back inside, meaning it happened at this point.
So what do that mean for the tent? Is it the same materials? Will it last better? Will that stitching pop?
The bag is a pretty important part to this set as you're going to want to store and carry this SUV Tent Car Camping Car Tent within it. So... it does concern us. BUT we THINK the tent itself is a better quality of stitching. Time will tell.

5. Ready for use
Pro: We both felt like the inside had some great room and that once we can step in, we're going to find it gives us everything we need and are looking for. Again, on this pavement and grassy area we used we did NOT want to cause damage - it also made us discuss having a ground cloth under it to help protect the tent materials.
So looking inside, spending some time discussing it, we feel like we're going to have the privacy we want, the shade we need in the summer sun, and the size that allows us to have chairs, food, and whatever we want.
The tent also gives us an option for car camping. We are NOT campers, but sometimes talk about going with my sister-in-law and her family and with the right mattress in the back of our Prius, we think it might be fun. This tent would give us that privacy and space for day time, but also something around us for nights. We actually are talking about giving it a try.

We did not put up the awning for the front, but it was nice giving the inside added privacy - it is attached to itself on the sides via velcro, then to the top as a permanent attachment - you add the included stacks and can have it up as an awning or keep it as-is and use it for the front of the tent, over the included netting. Really well designed idea.

So in the end, we both really like this SUV Tent Car Camping Car Tent. It was very much or at least very similar to what we had been thinking and looking for. Something for the car, gives us privacy, shade, and potential for car camping. Easy to set up. Looks nice. Great space inside.

The reason for the 4 stars over the 5 is that 1. the bag tore on first returning of the tent to the bag. 2. The back side hole. It would be much better to have something like the netting at least to give that side some closure. 3. Better instructions would be helpful.

But in the end we both love this SUV Tent Car Camping Car Tent and if it lasts (much longer than the bag) we will be thrilled with the find - we are already, but... - and feel like we are going to get some great use out of it.

Still waterproof, still gets dropped occasionally and comes back for more. I've worn most of the anodizing off down to bare aluminum. It's not a flamethrower, but for 99% of my needs, 80 lumens for 5+ hours is way more useful than 1500 lumens for 10 minutes. This light just keeps on trucking.

2/20/18 Still going strong, my everyday carry light.

1/16/17 Bumped up to 5 stars, the replacement light has been perfect. I lubed the tailcap threads and O-ring with petroleum jelly as soon as I received it, this might help.

11/15/16 Colorful Days replaced the light even though it was beyond the warranty period, quite nice of them. Will see how long this one lasts. Back up to three stars for now.

11/7/16 Downgraded to one star. Light flickers and is quite dim. Reacts to tailcap being unscrewed or tightened, and sometimes only works after loosening the tailcap slightly. Poor connection between tailcap and body of the light - useless.

So far so good. Solid little light and significantly less expensive than the Fenix and 4Sevens and Zebralight flashlights I keep losing. Headband is comfortable. The little case is nice enough but no one is ever going to keep the light in it - 5x more bulky than the light and headband alone.

With the cost reduction vs the brands mentioned above, some compromises are made. While it runs on rechargeable batteries, it's not really happy doing so. Much dimmer. I don't think the regulation circuitry likes the lower voltage much vs primaries much. The claim of 150 lumens is a joke, WAG compared to other lights I have, I would put this at ~80 lumens.

Can't comment on durability or waterproofness yet.

So far, while I'm happy with the light for the money, there's a reason I bought higher end lights. If my better lights don't turn up soon I'll just buy another one and this light will eventually get relegated to backup duty.

text_fidelity_a:
Leg Shield Reflective Ankle Bands - Very Large Reflective Area for Greater Visibility - Bright, Comfortable, Neoprene - Straps for Biking, Running, Walking - Protects Cyclist's Pants from Chain First off, these are by far the brightest reflective anything I've ever bought, and I've bought >20 wrist bands, arm bands, leg bands, vests, .... Photons apparently hate this material: every single photon that hits it immediately turns right around and heads back where it came from. You will be seen when you're wearing these. They're so bright you may be seen from space. :)

Second, customer service can't be beat. I ordered both the the wrist bands and the leg bands, but only received the wrist bands. I contacted the vendor, Mark, and he sent the leg bands out within 12 hours of receiving my email. Later I had a problem with the reflective material separating from the neoprene on one one of the wrist bands, and Mark didn't just replace the one that failed, he sent me a whole new pair, and very quickly. So this is a low-risk purchase: if you have any issues, Mark will make it right for you.

One thing I'm not fond of is that the hook portion of the hook and loop closure is too long. Unless the band fits perfectly around your leg, a good sized section of the hook portion will be exposed, and can snag on cyclists' lycra gear. I wish the hook portion was just an inch long. The 3" loop portion would still allow a couple of inches of flexibility re length.

Also, I'm not sure why these have both extra long hook and loop closures and are made of stretchy neoprene. Both seem intended to allow the band to fit different diameters of legs + clothing, so I'm not sure why you need both. And the stretchy neoprene makes it much more likely that the relatively delicate reflective material will separate from it, as happened with 1 of the 4 bands I originally purchased. I'd prefer the fabric to not stretch to minimize the risk of failure, and just use the velcro to adjust the length. But since Mark backs up the product if it fails, this is a small deal.

Overall, I'm happy with these. I believe they're the brightest reflective bands you can buy, so if you want to be seen, these will do the job.
text_fidelity_b: Leg Shield Reflective Ankle Bands - Very Large Reflective Area for Greater Visibility - Bright, Comfortable, Neoprene - Straps for Biking, Running, Walking - Protects Cyclist's Pants from Chain

text_fidelity_a: Klean Kanteen Wide Mouth Single Wall Stainless Steel Water Bottle with Leak Proof Stainless Steel Interior Cap - 40oz - Brushed Stainless I don't know how to rate the sturdiness or durability of such a product.  It's a steel bottle.  If you drop it, particularly when full, you'll put some dents in it.  If you're planning on driving over it with a tank, maybe just get a polycarbonate Nalgene.. And I can't really speak to using this on a campfire, which i know some folks do out in the wild.  What i can say is that I really like this bottle.  It has one flaw:  I'm not a huge fan of the cap.  The cap threads onto external threading and this snugs the lip of the bottle up against a gasket seated in the cap.  If this gasket isn't properly seated, the bottle leaks and more than a couple of times have I thought I closed the cap tightly ( you kind of have to crank it down due to this design) only to realize that, though I had, the gasket was allowing water to slowly leak out.  This is a problem on leather car seats or even in a pack, and though I haven't had any major property loss as a result, i still check this bottle for leaks before i stow it.  Say what you will about Nalgene bottles, but they simply don't have this issue.  Nor does the TKWide line, with an internal threading and o-ring cap, made by this same company..  The gasket itself is removable and i think the tab (which is how you pull the gasket out) might get caught in the lip of the bottle occasionally.  Anyway, I do quite like this bottle and I use it almost everyday now, though I've gotten in to the habit of checking it for leaks every time i use it.
text_fidelity_b: Klean Kanteen Wide Mouth Single Wall Stainless Steel Water Bottle with Leak Proof Stainless Steel Interior Cap - 40oz - Brushed Stainless

text_fidelity_a:
Milliard Golf Organizer - Extra Large Size - Fit 2 Golf Bags and Other Golfing Equipment and Accessories in This Handy Storage Rack - Great Gift Item I put this together in about an hour while watching a movie in the man cave. So basically it could go together a little quicker if you keep yourself organized. I recommend that you do the following . Remove all the pieces from packaging (assuring that you have all you are supposed to have). Match up all the screws and nuts to make sure you have good thread matching. This keeps you from dropping them and/or losing track in the midst of the assembly. The instructions are not the best I have seen but they do give you enough information to get the job done. The pieces seem to me to only have one way to put them together and if you have a remote idea (remember the instructions) it should go together rather quickly. Avoid tightening the nuts and screws completely until you have the all the screws and bolts for the pieces you are working on in place. When you do snug them up and move to the next piece. A couple of them will make you wish for a third arm but if you have someone there to lend a hand on the trickier ones, it should be a breeze. I was working on a carpeted area so I did some flipping around to help give me the angles I wanted. The carpet allowed me not to worry about scratching the floor or the metal. After putting this together, I think I could put one together in about twenty minutes without distraction.
I like the look of the organizer and it had plenty of room for my old Mizuno cart bag and my new Sun Mountain cart bag. It seems like it will be plenty durable although I guess that remains to be seen over time. It was light to move around (unloaded). I am most pleased with the end product.
text_fidelity_b: Milliard Golf Organizer - Extra Large Size - Fit 2 Golf Bags and Other Golfing Equipment and Accessories in This Handy Storage Rack - Great Gift Item

text_fidelity_a:
Lightspeed Outdoors 2 Person PVC-Free Air Bed Mattress for Camping and Travel i have bought some really expensive beds over the past few years and i have done much research to get a good bed. i have not succeeded. so i decided to go with this. TPU does not stretch as many commented on and so it stays inflated. i put a foam 2" topper on top of this and it's like a regular bed, but i think it is better. yes the inflator pump sucks but it does the job. i am not going back to a normal bed. just have to dial in the air pressure now for the ideal feel. i wish i had not spent all that money on the last bed. worth noting that the size can be an issue when fitting sheets. it's in between double and queen size. consider jersey sheets in double since they stretch.

update
ok so the negative vote i got made me think and i realize most of the review is about how regular beds suck and not how this bed is awesome, so time for an update. one of the great features i already mentioned, no stretching or leaks so the bed stays firm. another good feature is the connections inside the bed. the system they use allows for a fairly flat surface because the seal points are not form top to bottom but have a linkage that allows the bed to inflate to a fairly consistent depth across the surface. the image shows it well. other air beds have deep pockets where the weld connects the top to bottom piece. that is a major deal if you have ever slept on an airbed like this. flat surface is key. this bed seems to have the most advanced welding. the only real issue i have is that the bed is so light weight that it moves around easily on the frame. that can be annoying. Costco sells this same item and i sell to Costco so i know how intensely they review items for consideration to sell. this is the best airbed on the market today, period.
text_fidelity_b: Lightspeed Outdoors 2 Person PVC-Free Air Bed Mattress for Camping and Travel

text_fidelity_a:
YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment for Gym - Anti-Slip 36" Tricep Rope Pull Down Attachment Unique Rubber Grip for Full Palm Support, Pulley System LAT Pulldown Cable Machine Attachments My wife and I prefer weights as a workout, but both of us find the handles our community provides for the lat pull to be uncomfortable. The community provides the bar and nylon strap options, but 1. even with leather gloves they are uncomfortable, and 2. as a shorter guy my arm span is not such that I can get and maintain a comfortable reach (I can't hold the rubber grips on the bar), so for safety and comfort, I'm outta luck. But when I saw this YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment for the gym I thought it might help me with comfort and safety, and be something she and I could both use to help improve.

The YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment is as easy as any attachment for the lat pull to get on and off, fitting the community's machine easily. There is a concern we have, but only time will tell if it plays out: the connection has a plastic exterior over what appears to be a metal disk, but we cannot tell how far that metal extends. It SEEMS as though it is only a disk and that the majority of the top piece is plastic. So we are not sure for how long or how much weight this connector will last. It is not that we have "proof" of it being subpar, just concerning by appearance.

The material of the rope itself also seems, not as overall strong, but as we are not at all experts in these materials or what is common in most of the heavy work gyms, we have nothing to compare it to. So we are going with it being an appropriate set up and provided materials. For our level of weights, even as I get stronger, we don't see it being at all an issue.

Lastly is the YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment's handgrip, where you get that ergonomic element. I attempt to show in the various images how it is structured, curveted for the hand to rest within, allowing for a strong and comfortable grip. Again, I'm a shorter guy, so I also have a smaller hand. My wife's fingers are slightly longer than mine. We each find that the grip is both good and bad. We can each grip it and feel we have a secure hold. We feel safe. We feel a great pull. However, we each have a spot on the grip where it cuts into our finger/hand and begins to rub. In two images I show 1. the grip itself as I hold it up, then 2. my thumb over the top - it is at this point for me where it rubs and begins to feel like it's cutting into the thumb. Again, it is my hand size. My wife's issue is in the palm. She can fully and comfortably grip the handle, but at the base of the palm there is a cutting pressure.

So, do we like the YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment? Yes, very much.
In spite of the issue and admittedly, with only using it twice for our full reps, we do like it. I will add, we have not worn our gloves during these workouts. We normally do, but circumstances had us in there without them, so using our bare hands, we did come up with discomfort whereby we got through the workouts, but didn't go full out as the discomfort grew. BUT, we both feel like once we have on the leather gloves the issue will at the least decrease greatly enough so as to allow us a full on workout and be okay. I will update if that does not pan out. But for each of us, the better grip and the overall feel of the YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment as far as what we can do, how safe we feel, and even comfort to the greater part of our hands is enough. We went with the 4 star because of the issue, but WE THINK THAT if they were to add a more comfortable cushion (rubber, something) to the grip, this would be a great 5 star grip.
text_fidelity_b: YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment for Gym - Anti-Slip 36" Tricep Rope Pull Down Attachment Unique Rubber Grip for Full Palm Support, Pulley System LAT Pulldown Cable Machine Attachments

text_fidelity_a:
OKAI EA10 Electric Scooter with Seat, Up to 25-35 Miles Range & 15.5MPH, Moped Scooter Bike for Adults with 10 Inch Vacuum Tires Set up of the scooter is a fairly simple process. The only downside is putting on the bike seat. It doesn’t slide down very easily and isn’t fully secure, the seat swivels back and forth which can be inconvenient.

The scooter in general is great and able to take me from point A to point B in a timely manner. One feature that really makes the scooter user friendly is the battery. Being able to take the battery out and leave the scooter outside while charging it inside is extremely convenient.

The keys that come with the scooter are also extremely convenient. With the NFC feature it’s easy to unlock, all you have to do is touch the key to the scooter’s digital interface.

Making sure you have enough battery is important if you are planning on going somewhere far. The gauge on the scooter doesn’t give you an accurate idea of how far you can go, and the apps percentages aren’t very accurate either.

One other thing I wish it had was a longer pole. It is tall enough for my hand to reach it when I’m standing but it has to be fully extended so it can be awkward and unsafe. If it was a little bit longer, it’d be perfect for sitting and standing.

It is most comfortable to ride while sitting but you are able to stand. Depending on your height, standing may feel comfortable or a bit awkward. If you’re around the 6ft range it feels slightly too short to use while standing, although it is possible. Both knives arrived oiled with the blades sharp. Each knife also has a drilled hole near the handle end for a lanyard if desired. Both of these are full tang knives and share a heavy duty sheath each having its own fitted sleeve/sheath. I had a hard time at first getting them in and out of the sheaths because of how tight they were, but the sheaths do start to loosen up as you remove the knifes and insert them back into the sheaths. The larger knife weighs 1 lb, 11 oz. The smaller knife weighs 7.3 oz. Both knives with the sheath have a combined weight of 2 lb, 10 oz. The sheath fits over a belt, and the belt strap is quite wide and looks to me like it should fit over most belt widths. At first I thought the sheath for the smaller knife could be detached by perhaps a snap or velcro, but the smaller knife sheath is strongly attached to the large sheath.

The only issue I found was along the outer edge of the smaller knife handle where the blade runs through the handle. The metal wasn't fully smooth and had what felt like microscopic burrs along the edge. I was able to smooth this with a super fine nail file, but had to be very careful in doing so such that I would not sand any of the wood on the handle. This only took me about a minute to do, but had to be done.

Aside from the little issue mentioned above which I was able to easily fix, I really love this set. Both knifes and sheaths are super strong, heavy duty and well-constructed. Great addition to any knife collection!

is it good or bad?

I've been looking for a well-made compartmentalized military shoulder bag that I can hang on a hook by the door and grab on the way out should some type of SHTF. It needs to be tough and durable, have expandable pockets and compartments, and be able to carry a bunch of things that I need to take with me to cover short-term needs. In hot and humid Southwest Florida that includes: extra carbine mags, a suppressed .22LR with mags, flashlight with extra batteries, water filter, MREs, mosquito net and insect repellent, a short tactical hatchet, a fixed blade and folding knife, duct tape, a Toptool 14 in 1 (multitool), matches, meds, hearing aid batteries and cleaning kit, first aid kit, and some energy bars. That's quite a bit of "stuff" but it all fits in this bag.

Even though the bag is weighted down with all of this gear, the heavy Oxford Nylon, double stitching, and robust zippers and clips should do the trick. The nylon has a waterproof coating and the shoulder strap is padded and fully adjustable for comfort. There are enough compartments/pockets to keep your items separated and easy to get to. Properly packed, you should be able to minimize any rubbing or clanking sound that might result, and each compartment has either a zipper, pinch fastener, or drawstring to keep things from flying out of the pack while you're on the move.

The configuration of this bag should prove useful for several different applications other than what I am using it for. I did notice a few cosmetic errors in the construction but nothing that will compromise this product. While I couldn't find any country of manufacture on the bag, they do offer a 100% satisfaction guarantee, a 30 day money back refund or exchange, and also advertise 24 hour customer service.

text_fidelity_a:
NTK Cherokee GT 8 to 9 Person 10 by 12 Foot Outdoor Dome Family Camping Tent 100% Waterproof 2500mm, Easy Assembly, Durable Fabric Full Coverage Rainfly I'm an Eagle Scout. We go Jeeping a lot. As an adult, we take our kids camping a LOT.

We've had this tent for 2 1/2 years and taken it camping probably 15-20 times. It's been all over the desert of NM, the mountains of Colorado, and the red rocks of Utah.

This tent is AWESOME.

PROS:
- Dome design doesn't require stakes in the ground - we have a lot of rocks up in the mountains.
- Dome design is super simple and quick to put up - usually about 2 minutes for us if we're taking our time.
- Walled sides - with the tub shape, water never gets in.
- It's HUGE. We usually put a full size air mattress AND two twin size mattresses in it PLUS there's about enough room for another twin mattress as well. We could probably fit two queen mattresses in there.
- It's TALL - my wife and I are both 6ft tall and can stand up in the middle very easily, not the "standing up but hunched over kind of" actually standing upright.
- The BAG IS AWESOME - hate trying to get a tent back into it's bag? This is the tent for you! Fold it into quarters, roll it up around the poles, throw it in, and because the bag is a little bigger than you need, it fits easily. (No, it's not loose and baggy, just right). We've had nights of "quick, just shove it in the bag" and it fits fine that way too. Easy to put away.
- HUGE POLES - you won't believe it till you see it, these poles are about as big around as a finger, not the little wimpy poles.
- BIG VENTS AND GIANT RAIN FLY - The vents on the sides are basically everything from the tub up to the top, so lots of ventilation. The Rain fly easily covers the mesh though and we've never had rain get in at all.
- No stakes necessary - we never use stakes, and the fly doesn't go anywhere and the tent stays put. We've shoved gear in the corners or occasionally a big rock, and done really well with this.

CONS:
- We had one of the bungee strings break in the poles, but that's to be expected after some use. It was easy enough to fix. The overall design is sturdy enough we used it a few times with no bungee at all and it was ok.
- Cooler weather - it has huge vents on the sides under the fly, so heat gets out when it's cold. But, we've also shoved a blanket or one of those two person hammocks between the tent and the fly and that helps keep the heat in a little better. Let's just say, it's probably not any colder than most other tents like this.
- Size. It is big, and if you need space to sprawl it's there. But if it's a cramped area because of trees, it is pretty big. If you're out west, and there's lots of room, this is a great tent.

CONCLUSION:
I've owned a 6-8 different tents, most of them dome tents, and this one is the toughest built, the most well-thought out, and the easiest to work with. I'd definitely buy this tent again.

(and if you have the space in your vehicle, throw some of those foam puzzle floor pieces in the tent and it makes it really, really posh)

(No, I didn't get this tent for free or anything, bought it outright).
text_fidelity_b: NTK Cherokee GT 8 to 9 Person 10 by 12 Foot Outdoor Dome Family Camping Tent 100% Waterproof 2500mm, Easy Assembly, Durable Fabric Full Coverage Rainfly

text_fidelity_a:
NSD Power AutoStart Spinner Gyroscopic Wrist and Forearm Exerciser with Auto Start Feature Of all the things I saw at CES, this was the only item I decided to buy. I actually found their competitor, DynaFlex Powerball first but decided to go with the NSD Spinner brand instead because it sounded like they were more on top of customer service. I also liked that they had an affordable wind up version that didn't require using the cord. You wind it up by turning the ball in the direction of the arrow (see picture attached, the arrow is embossed into the green part.) I'd read these kinds of balls were popular with rock climbers as a forearm exercise and it was fun to use, so I decided to give it a shot

Pros:
- Don't have to worry about losing a cord. You can take this thing with you anywhere and give it a spin.
- Easy to use - I find myself picking this up while I'm watching TV or just walking around.
- Helps with wrist / forearm pain - I have pretty bad pain from using the computer too much, and I found using the ball helped me stretch my forearms and hands and helped reduce the pain a lot
- I can't validate, but when I have the ball spinning on high RPMS it takes a lot of effort to maintain my grip on the ball so I feel like I'm doing something to build up my strength.

Cons:
- If you have sweaty hands like I do, it's sometimes tough to wind up the ball
- Very confusing lineup of options. I recognize in the end reading and taking note of the titles is super important. Here's an overview of the lineup -

~$20 : NSD Power Essential Spinner
= regular ball, no counter to show rpms, no self starter, vibration free to 15,000 RPM

~$30 : NSD Power AutoStart Spinner Gyroscopic Wrist and Forearm Exerciser with Auto Start Feature
= regular ball, no counter to show rpms, w/ self start, vibration free to 15,000 RPM

~$40 : NSD Power Winners Roll and Spin Spinner Gyroscopic Wrist and Forearm Exerciser with Digital LCD Counter and Auto-Start Feature
= ball w/ rpm meter, w/self start, vibration free to 15,000 RPM **what I got**

~$50 : NSD Roll 'N Spin Rainbow Lit AutoStart Spinner Gyroscopic Wrist and Forearm Exerciser with AutoStart and Multi-Lit LED =
= ball no counter to show rpm, w/ self starter, has LED lights that light up to different colours depending on how fast you're spinning, vibration free to 15,000 RPM

~$75 : NSD Power Winner's Precision Sterling Spinner Gyroscopic Wrist (SILVER COLOUR)
= ball w/rpm meter, NO self starter. Vibration free to 15,000 RPM. Delivers more resistance than the plastic balls. Inertial resistance: 19kg at 10,000rpm (350Hz) 3.2kg at 10,000rpm (450Hz) "up to 41.3lbs"

~$75: NSD Power Ultimate Winner's Precision Sterling Spinner Gyroscopic Wrist (GOLD COLOUR)
= ball w/rpm meter, NO self starter. Designed to deliver higher RPMS. Claims vibration free operation at up to 27,000 RPM.

Overall, since these aren't expensive, it was worth it for me to try out.

Update: I still love this ball but I recommend not leaving it anywhere really hot. Since I take this ball with me everywhere, I'd left it in the car overnight in the hot summer weather and I think the glue that held the grip band to the ball melted. Now I can't keep the rubber grip on the ball when I spin as easily.
text_fidelity_b: NSD Power AutoStart Spinner Gyroscopic Wrist and Forearm Exerciser with Auto Start Feature

I understand the reasoning - "technology changes fast and we want you to have the most up to date instructions." Okay, but sadly the instructions did not match the version of the device that I had, so I had to figure out some of it on my own. I mean you'd think they would keep the online instructions up to date if that's the reason they want you to go online to get them. I would have appreciated a brief "quick start" paper instruction inside the box.

Okay, enough about the instructions. Once I figured it out, this little device collected flawless from my iphone although you need to keep the app active or else the device shuts down. think of it as an extension of your iphone screen - a second monitor. I also have a Garmin heart rate monitor (ANT+) and a Garmin speed/cadence sensor (ANT+) on my bike. the Wahoo found both of those quickly and displayed the data accurately. I matched it against my Garmin 310XT watch and it matched up perfectly.

The one thing I had to remember was to start the app on the phone in order to get the distance and time to start recording! I was cruising along and watching my heart rate and cadence but couldn't figure out why the mileage wasn't getting logged until I realized I hadn't started things up on the iPhone. So this works well, and if you've already got other apps and like using your iphone then this is a great little device.

We live in a warm weather state and time at the pool and beach is a must. But that also means exposure to sun both directly and indirectly. I have sensitive skin - and we all need to be careful of sun exposure - so I learned from my dad to wear a hat as often as you can. I gabbed this Fishing Hat Sun Hat with Sunscreen and UV Protection to protect my head and face and so far, it’s working great. I like the color - it’s a black, though not stark, but a bit of a “faded” black. I do not need this - I’ve got a pretty big head - but if my wife were to borrow it she might - we have not used this option yet. I’ve worn it in the pool and it worked great. It cannot protect from the reflective light, but it keeps the sun off my head and that’s what I’m looking for - and for that it worked perfectly. I do take the “strap” and tuck in up over the sides and into the tightener strap at the back to keep it out of the way. If you needed it for keeping the hat on, however, it’s there. Overall this is a nice hat and I’m really glad I got it. I will most certainly get a lot of use out of this Fishing Hat Sun Hat with Sunscreen and UV Protection.

text_fidelity_a:
Atlas 2008 Women's Elektra 11 Series Snowshoe I am adding this paragraph after three trips. The bindings have lots of rivets, and
I wondered about their durability. After the third trip, when I took off the shoes,
one of the rivets holding the heel strap broke. Fortunately I was back at the car;
if some of the rivets fail out on the trail, the shoe could become useless. Other
reviews that I have seen have not mentioned a problem with durability, but now I
wonder. The rest of the review hasn't changed.

This snowshoe has lots of good points. The only negative, and the reason that I did
not give it 5 stars, is a lack of flotation. I cannot compare it to other snowshoes
of the "modern" solid decking type, or the "traditional" wood frame lattice decking,
though it seems to have less flotation than my traditional shoes. I got the 27"
model, and with pack I weigh under 165 lbs; the shoes are rated to 200 lbs or more.
In a soft, old snow, I sank in 8-12" breaking trail; sometimes I sank in more.

The shoe has some very good points. The bindings are secure and comfortable, and
they won't ruin your leather boots or give you blisters by clamping down on the top
of your toes. The traction is good. The toes snap up automatically, and you can walk
with a pretty normal stride. Because of the short distance between your toes and
the toes of the shoes, the lack of a long tail, and the crampons, you can climb
over deadfall very easily. There's no need to back up to free your toes, burying
your tail in the process. I like the heel lift, though I only tried it briefly.
The lift bars are very stiff to put back down. The shoes are lightweight and don't
carry lots of snow on their tops, so you don't have to lift lots of weight with
each step. The natural stride and light weight tend to offset the less than ideal
flotation.

Pros:
Excellent binding system, excellent or very good traction, very good walking
stride, light weight

Cons:
Flotation may be somewhat lacking - I can't compare to other shoes, just to an
ideal, which is not possible to achieve
text_fidelity_b: Atlas 2008 Women's Elektra 11 Series Snowshoe

text_fidelity_a:
Large 35L Hiking Backpack - Packable Lightweight Travel Backpack Daypack Water Resistant Cycling Hicking Small Outdoor Backpack Women Men I admit I am slow to write reviews. I want to see how a product holds up in the long haul.

This HEXIN 35L pack has held up and performed wonderfully!!!

Initially I purchased this to take with me to Ireland because I wanted to do a lot of exploring without dragging around large amounts of bags to encompass my gear. It was still in its comfy EASY TO USE self-pouch when I got to the Emerald Isle.

The first day I really used it was a lovely rainy Irish morning. I put all my gear in, from sensitive electronics to water bottles in the side pouches (hugely helpful to not have to dig in bag for a drink). Stored my inn keys and passport in the inner pocket where they were safe but not easily removed from my pack without notice.

I carried my larger Pixelbook, cameras and assortments; Change of clothes and extra layers to add or shed as needed; snacks and even an extra pair of hike boots in the bottom in case I didn't want to tromp around in wet boots.

There are so many pockets and secure dividers. This pack is well made. I have (before and since) tried a variety of styles and brands and I only swear by Hexin. It has lasted two full years and is still water resistant (and been through a LOT of rain), the zippers are still strong and safely covered. I can be really rough on gear, but I clean it after each adventure and I have had NO issues.

There is also a bright orange whistle which, I have only used for my dog, but is great for a small woman to have in emergency.

I love that I can also stick stuff in the straps in the mesh pockets and under the elastic band. You never know.

The straps and pack are nicely designed so they are always comfortable no matter what I stuff in the bag,

I love that when I am not using it I can fold it down so small that it lays flat in the bottom of my bag.

I am back to purchase another HEXIN now because I have given up on the rest. This is a really great bag. At 35L it holds more than enough gear, clothes, etc., and keeps things protected. I highly recommend it and that does not come lightly.

Bottom line: BEST BAG EVER!!!
text_fidelity_b: Large 35L Hiking Backpack - Packable Lightweight Travel Backpack Daypack Water Resistant Cycling Hicking Small Outdoor Backpack Women Men

I took this megaphone over to the lady who runs the horse ranch because that is how she imparts instructions to the folks who come to ride her horses on the trails.  I know this because I hear her on her own megaphone every day!  Megaphones are meant for talking to a crowd and while I am not often trying to talk to a crowd, my neighbor is (in a sense).  She was thrilled to try this one out and found the usb prepared content ability was perfect as there are things she says as they move along the trails - so regularly that having it programmed to say it saves her voice at the end of the day.  That is the same with the ability to record when she has special groups and using their group's name during the talks she gives on the megaphone helps her to acknowledge special groups.  I had meant for her to just test it out for me, but she was so taken with it that I now have a standing invitation to come ride the trails while she uses the megaphone!

Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in)) I've been using a Fitbit One for years now. Really love it. But I wanted to get the pulse tracking feature, so purchased the Charge HR recently.

I do love it for the HR monitor, and sleep tracking is a lot easier on the HR (having to put on that wristband to track via the One was an added annoyance). And the caller ID feature is cool.

But there are two things I don't like as well. First, I have a very petite wrist (small bone/frame). The Charge HR looks huge on my wrist, and really doesn't sit well. The inflexible part with the face sticks out beyond my wrist, where on someone with a bigger wrist it would flex where it needs to bend around. Hard to explain!

The other thing, which is probably related, is that when I wear a winter coat, the sleeve pushes the FB down on my wrist where it digs in and hurts.

This isn't significant unless you are competing against others rather than just against yourself like I do, but I think the Charge HR counts more steps than my One does. I haven't changed my routine, but I find I'm hitting my 10,000 much earlier in the day than before.

Oh, and I have to charge the HR more frequently than I did the One.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in))
